privacy.note: AI Reply does not read your conversations in other messengers by itself. The operating system does not allow that, and we do not claim otherwise: the keyboard only sees the text you copied or selected yourself.
privacy.p1.body: Neither the copied message nor the generated reply is written to the database — only a reply you choose to send with a report.
privacy.p1.title: Conversations are not stored
privacy.p2.body: The admin panel has no "view conversations" screen, because there is nothing to show.
privacy.p2.title: Administrators cannot read them
privacy.p3.body: Logs hold metadata only: time, duration, token counts, error code.
privacy.p3.title: Logs carry no text
privacy.p4.body: No contact list, no location, no advertising identifier.
privacy.p4.title: No extra data is collected
privacy.subtitle: Writing a reply needs the text on our server and at OpenAI. Our server does not store it.
privacy.title: Privacy is in the architecture, not in a promise
sim.admin.demo_account_note: A single dedicated account backs every generation made in this simulator. Its quota and usage are real.
sim.admin.demo_note: The user list and the charts on this page are seeded demo records — real customer data is never shown in a demo. The plan catalogue and the system status below are read from the live backend.
sim.admin.lede: What the business side looks like: who is using the product, how much, on what plan, at what cost.
sim.admin.title: Admin dashboard
sim.android.lede: The same product with Android conventions — Material dialogs, the system keyboard picker, and the voice instruction that is unique to Android.
sim.android.title: Android simulator
sim.arch.admin_detail: Daily limits live in the database, so raising 30 to 50 is an admin action, not an app release. Every change is written to the audit log.
sim.arch.admin_never: No admin screen can show the text of a conversation.
sim.arch.android_detail: The same product as an Android input method, plus on-device speech recognition for dictating the instruction.
sim.arch.android_never: Never uploads audio; only recognised text is sent.
sim.arch.auth_detail: Registration is by phone number with a one-time code; admin sessions use PBKDF2 password hashes and server-side session records.
sim.arch.auth_never: Passwords are never stored in plain text, and OTP attempts are rate-limited.
sim.arch.context_detail: The profile is loaded on the server and turned into named data blocks in the prompt: business context, rules, and the user's instruction, each introduced as data rather than as orders.
sim.arch.context_never: A copied message saying 'ignore previous instructions' is quoted, not obeyed.
sim.arch.gateway_detail: One place builds the prompt, calls the provider, counts tokens and estimates cost. Everything the mobile apps see comes through it.
sim.arch.gateway_never: Neither the incoming message nor the generated reply is written anywhere.
sim.arch.ios_detail: The app holds the account and preferences; the keyboard extension does the work inside other apps. They share a keychain group, so signing in once is enough.
sim.arch.ios_never: Holds no provider key and never calls OpenAI.
sim.arch.lede: Select any component to see what it does, where it lives and — just as important — what it never does.
sim.arch.limits_detail: Quota is reserved atomically before OpenAI is called and refunded if the call fails, so parallel requests cannot oversubscribe a plan and a failed reply is never charged.
sim.arch.limits_never: The client's own count is never trusted.
sim.arch.limits_sub: Quota reserved before the provider call
sim.arch.openai_detail: The provider is called from the backend with the key from the server environment. The model is fixed by the server; the client cannot choose it.
sim.arch.openai_never: The key is never present in any app bundle, APK or IPA.
sim.arch.privacy_body: There is no column for it in the schema, no field for it in the admin API, and nothing of it in the logs. A test sends a unique string through the API and fails the build if it appears in the database file, the WAL or the logs.
sim.arch.storage_detail: Accounts, plans, subscriptions, quota counters and usage events. Usage events record length, tokens, latency and status — never content.
sim.arch.storage_never: There is no column for message text.
sim.arch.title: System architecture
sim.arch.transport_detail: Every call carries a short-lived access token. Refresh tokens rotate and reuse is detected, so a stolen token has a small window and leaves a trace.
sim.arch.transport_never: No long-lived token is stored on the device unencrypted.

sim.overview.lede: See how AI Reply turns an incoming customer message into a context-aware reply, straight from the keyboard — on a real backend, with real limits.
sim.overview.p1_body: AI Reply is not another chat app. It is an intelligent layer inside the apps people already use, so nothing about their workflow changes.
sim.overview.p2_body: Tone, audience, language and business context are stored per account and applied to every reply, so the same question gets a different answer for a florist and for a law firm.
sim.overview.p3_body: The app never talks to OpenAI. It talks to the AI Reply backend, which holds the key, enforces the quota and stores no message text at all.
sim.overview.p3_title: The key stays on the server
sim.overview.title: Experience AI Reply

sim.wf.context_body: Quota is reserved before anything else, then the saved profile becomes named data blocks in the prompt.

delete.title: Delete your AI Reply account
delete.intro: AI Reply is an AI keyboard for iPhone and Android that helps you write replies in messengers. Here you can delete your AI Reply account together with the data our server keeps about it.
delete.app_body: Open AI Reply, go to Settings → Account → Delete account and confirm. The account is deleted right away. If you signed in with Apple, the iPhone asks you to confirm with your Apple ID, so that we can also disconnect Sign in with Apple. You can always remove AI Reply yourself in your Apple ID settings under Sign in with Apple.
delete.app_body_apple_manual: Open AI Reply, go to Settings → Account → Delete account and confirm. The account is deleted right away. If you signed in with Apple, you can also remove AI Reply in your Apple ID settings under Sign in with Apple.
delete.data_body: Everything our server keeps about the account: the e-mail and sign-in methods (Apple, Google, e-mail), the profile (name, role, description, tone, business details, reply language and other settings), consent records, usage counters and request history, devices and push tokens, notification settings and notifications, app usage events, reports you sent and payment records. Deletion is immediate and cannot be undone. The texts you copied and the replies were never stored, so there is nothing to delete there.
delete.kept_body: Nothing that identifies you. The record of the app installation on your phone (platform, app and system version, device model) loses its link to the account and its push token, and is removed automatically {after} without use. The log of administrator actions may keep the random account number, without your e-mail or other details. The keyboard keeps working for typing.
delete.web_body: No longer have the app? Enter the e-mail of your AI Reply account. If an account with this e-mail exists, we send a code to it; enter the code here and the account is deleted.
delete.web_apple_note: Signed in with Apple and hid your e-mail? Enter the address Apple created for AI Reply — it is shown in your Apple ID settings under Sign in with Apple — or delete the account in the app.
delete.code_sent: If an account with this e-mail exists, we have sent a code to it. The code is valid for {minutes} minutes.
delete.confirm_note: Your account, profile, consents, usage history and devices are deleted from our server right away. This cannot be undone. The keyboard keeps working for typing.
delete.error.invalid_code: The code is not correct. Check it and try again.
delete.error.expired: This code no longer works. Request a new one.
delete.error.attempts: Too many attempts. Request a new code.
delete.error.rate_limited: Too many requests. Try again later.
delete.error.generic: Couldn't delete the account. Check the connection and try again.
support.title: Help and support
support.intro: AI Reply is an AI keyboard for iPhone and Android that helps you write replies in messengers. Here is how to reach us and where to find the documents.
support.help_keyboard: The keyboard does not appear: turn on AI Reply in the system keyboard settings and switch to it. On iPhone also allow Full Access — without it the keyboard cannot reach the server. The app shows these steps during setup.
support.help_limit: Replies stopped: the free plan has a daily limit. Replies come back the next day; the app and the keyboard show how many are left.
support.help_report: A reply is offensive, harmful or wrong: tap Report in AI Reply and choose the reason. Reports come to our team.
support.help_consent: To stop sending texts to OpenAI, withdraw AI consent in Settings → Privacy. To remove everything, delete the account.
